prize_parts.citation: For determining the atomic structure of nitrogenase and its iron-molybdenum cofactor, including the central carbide, which made the enzyme's N2 reduction chemistry accessible to physical analysis

statement.case_for: I have narrowed my own position after round 1. What is established about nitrogenase is its structure: Rees determined the MoFe and Fe protein structures and the cofactor environment, and Einsle resolved the cofactor at atomic resolution and assigned the central carbide. These results were confirmed independently and recently by cryo-EM of turnover states, they define the metal cluster whose chemistry every mechanistic discussion now starts from, and they concern the enzyme behind biological nitrogen fixation, the counterpart of Haber-Bosch. Stated this way the claim is one attributable discovery with two clear names, which answers the line-of-work objection I raised against my own candidacy. It is a physical statement about a catalytic metal cluster, which is the standard I apply to biological energy conversion.
statement.case_against: The reservation raised by Aili, Linke, Chabes, Somfai and Zou is correct: the catalytic cycle is not closed, the N2 binding mode and the redox states that bind substrate are unresolved, so this prize would honour structure and not an answer on mechanism. Narrowing to Rees and Einsle excludes Seefeldt, Dean and Ribbe, whose kinetic, genetic and biosynthetic work is substantial, and Dean and Ribbe have a real priority claim in cofactor assembly that the citation does not address. The candidate also has the thinnest support of any shortlisted idea for a first choice: one first place, mine, and four members ranking it at all. I cannot call my field affinity a committee consensus, and a structure-only prize could be judged a lesser result than the settled mechanism the committee would prefer to wait for.

responses.point: Please say what the committee could state as established in a one-sentence citation, and how the original structural discovery is separated from later cofactor and mechanistic refinements.
responses.response: This is the question that moved me. What can be stated as established is the atomic structure of the iron-molybdenum cofactor and its protein, including the central light atom identified as carbide, and that is the citation I now propose. Rees supplies the first structures and Einsle the atomic-resolution cofactor and the carbide assignment. Seefeldt's kinetic and spectroscopic work, and the Lowe-Thorneley framework beneath it, is mechanistic refinement and I now keep it outside the citation instead of crediting a mechanism that remains open. I accept that this is a narrower prize than my round-1 version.

responses.point: The Rees and Einsle structures are among the most convincing in bioinorganic chemistry, but the mechanism is still evolving, so the citation should say the prize honours structure, and Seefeldt versus Dean as the third name is unclear.
responses.response: I take your suggestion directly: the citation now says structure, and I removed the third seat instead of arguing between Seefeldt and Dean, since neither is needed to state what is settled. That also reduces the contested attribution to a pair. I am glad you would move B028 up under a structure-centred reading, but I note that this is your sixth choice and my first, and I do not read that as a majority.

responses.point: Nitrogenase explains a mechanism in nature and has not produced a new capability, so it fails the game-changer test and ranks below B011.
responses.response: I accept that B011 passes a test I do not pass on for B028, and my alternatives still list it. I would disagree on one point. A structure that fixes a cofactor chemists could not describe for decades is a capability of understanding, and it supports the nitrogen-fixation chemistry that synthetic catalysts try to imitate. But your point about evidence of consequence is fair: PROTACs have independent reproduction and many compounds in late trials, whereas the nitrogenase prize stays mainly on structure. We differ on weighting, and I do not claim the point is settled.

responses.point: The nitrogenase structural story is persuasive, but the catalytic cycle is unresolved, attribution is hard at three, and the methodological spread to other fields counts more for B011.
responses.response: Your attribution concern is the reason for my change to two names. On methodological spread I think you are right that B011 reaches further, and I agree a PROTAC prize would legitimately outweigh mine on that criterion. Where I stay different is on maturity: the nitrogenase structures are fully confirmed over many years, while for degraders you and Aqvist both concede that no approved drug exists and that the Handa, Ito and Gray cereblon line would be left outside a Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli citation. Neither of us has the regulatory facts to hand, and I do not claim to.

responses.point: The base-editing prize rests on a defined deaminase chemistry with Liu, Komor and Gaudelli as separable inventors, reproduced widely and now reaching patients.
responses.response: I raised the CRISPR proximity and Target-AID priority questions in round 1, and your trio is a defensible answer to the attribution half, since the cytosine and adenine editors are separable inventions, a fact I underweighted when I named Liu alone. I still want the expert evidence to state what chemical principle is new beyond a known deaminase fused to a programmable module, and the Kondo and Nishida priority to be examined before the trio is final. Of the Liu configurations, I would prefer yours to a Liu-only seat, and B007 stays my second alternative.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts a structure-centred citation for B028 when the catalytic mechanism and the N2 binding mode remain unresolved.
Whether leaving out Seefeldt, Dean and Ribbe is defensible to the nitrogenase community, particularly for cofactor biosynthesis.
Whether PROTAC and molecular-glue credit can be separated in B011, and whether the absence of an approved degrader makes it premature, a regulatory fact I cannot verify.
Whether Target-AID priority and the proximity of the 2020 CRISPR prize weaken B007 enough to matter.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with B028 or the alternatives: nitrogenase is bioinorganic and not my research, although I share biological energy-conversion and mechanistic interests with the field. Xiaodong Zou is a Stockholm University colleague, a collegial matter that is relevant only if B047 is under vote and is not a recusal ground. No change from round 1.
